patch.value: brief since redeclared host-owned --author global, failing registration on pm-cli 2026.7.27

pm-cli 2026.7.27 ships GH-719: the host rejects any extension command whose flags shadow a host-owned global flag. The 'brief since' command declared { long: "--author" }, so its registerCommand call failed and the command did not register against a real pm host. The existing test suite could not catch this because it activated through a real SDK harness that did not previously exercise host-owned flag rejection. Fix: drop the --author flag declaration from brief since and read the value from ctx.global.author instead, matching the existing ctx.global usage pattern. Also fixed the audit:prod script which used plain 'npm audit --omit=dev' instead of the 'env -u npm_config_allow_scripts npm audit --omit=dev --ignore-scripts' form required by project-scoped installs. Added a suite-wide guard test asserting no registered command redeclares any of the nine host-owned globals. Bumped pm-cli to 2026.7.27.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Verified: activation probe prints failed=[] against the real pm host engine. npm test: 138/138 pass including the new suite-wide guard test asserting no command redeclares any host-owned global. release:check green end to end (typecheck, build, test, audit:prod, pack:dry-run, changelog:check). The --author flag is read from ctx.global.author in brief since, and the example in the usage string remains valid since --author still works as a host-owned global.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Correction during review: the initial fix read pm's host-owned global --author as the filter, but that global means 'override mutation author for this invocation', not 'whose changes to show'. Agents routinely pass --author <agent-id>, which would have silently narrowed every brief to that agent's own changes. Replaced with a distinct --by flag preserving filter semantics, plus an integration regression test asserting global --author does NOT filter while --by does. Verified the test fails with the exact assertion when the fix is reverted.
